title: How switches work
keyIdea: A switch opens and closes a gap in a circuit. When the switch is closed, its metal parts touch, the circuit is complete and current flows, so a lamp lights or a buzzer sounds. When the switch is open, there is a gap, the circuit is broken and the current stops everywhere in the loop at once. In a simple series circuit the switch works wherever it is placed. Every switch at home, from a light switch to a doorbell, does this same job.
familyTip: Make a switch with a paper clip, two split pins or drawing pins, a battery, a bulb or buzzer and wires on a piece of card. Then hunt for switches around the house and sort them: ones that stay where you put them (light switch) and ones that spring back (doorbell, keyboard key).

visual.caption: Is the circuit complete or broken? Drag each to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: A torch slider pushed to off
A paper clip touching both pins
A paper clip swung off the pin
A door-mat alarm with nobody on it

lab.caption: Flagship lab: open and close the strip inside a switch, make a paper-clip switch, move a switch round a loop, try two switches and work three switches at home.

kid: A circuit is a loop. Current can only flow if the loop has no gaps.
A switch makes a gap and then closes it. Inside are bits of metal. When they touch, the switch is closed. The loop is whole, so the bulb lights.
When the metal bits move apart, the switch is open. Now there is a gap. The current stops all the way round, and the bulb goes off.
Open means off and closed means on. The switch can go anywhere in the loop. A light switch, a doorbell and a torch button all work like this.
adult: Ages 8 to 9. This is the Year 4 electricity objective in the National Curriculum in England: recognise that a switch opens and closes a circuit and link this to whether a lamp lights in a simple series circuit. Key words: circuit, complete circuit, switch, open, closed, gap, cell, battery, bulb, buzzer, wire, conductor, current.

A switch is a pair of conducting contacts that can be joined or separated. Closed, it joins the loop so current flows; open, an air gap breaks it. In a series loop the current is the same all the way round, so it stops everywhere at once when any gap opens. A switch does not store or make electricity; the cell provides the push. Push switches (doorbells, keyboard keys) spring open when released; toggle switches stay put.

Common mistakes: thinking 'open' means on, as with a door; thinking the switch must sit next to the battery or before the bulb; thinking current still flows up to the gap or in the wire before the switch; and thinking a switch makes or stores electricity.

In the lab your child presses the metal strip inside a switch, builds a paper-clip switch for a buzzer, opens one switch in three places round the loop, tries all four settings of two switches, and works a light switch, a doorbell and a door-mat alarm.

practice.prompt: The switch in a circuit is open. What does the bulb do?
practice.hint: An open switch leaves a gap. Can the current get round a loop with a gap?
practice.explain: Open means there is a gap, so the circuit is broken. No current flows and the bulb is off.

practice.prompt: A loop has {a} switches in a row with one bulb. How many of them must be closed for the bulb to light?
practice.hint: Any open switch leaves a gap. How many gaps can there be if the bulb lights?
practice.explain: All {a} must be closed. One open switch anywhere breaks the loop.

practice.prompt: Why is the moving part inside a switch made of metal?
practice.hint: The moving part has to join the gap. What must it let through?
practice.explain: Metal is a conductor, so when it touches the contact, current can flow across the join.

practice.prompt: You press a doorbell {a} times. Each time, the push switch closes and then springs open. How many times does the circuit get completed?
practice.hint: Each press closes the gap once.
practice.explain: {a} presses close the circuit {a} times. It opens again each time you let go.

practice.prompt: The switch is after the bulb in the loop. You open it. What happens?
choices: Only half the bulb goes off
practice.hint: Try the switch in the 'after the bulb' box in the lab.
practice.explain: A gap anywhere in a simple loop stops the current all the way round, so the bulb goes off.

pool.prompt: What does a switch do in a circuit?
choices: It opens or closes a gap
pool.hint: Think of the metal strip in the lab. What did it do when you pressed it?
pool.explain: A switch joins or breaks the path. The cell gives the push; the switch only opens or closes the gap.

pool.hint: Closed means the metal parts touch. Is the loop whole then?
pool.explain: Closed means the gap is joined, so current flows. Open is off.

pool.prompt: Where can you put one switch in a simple loop so it turns the bulb on and off?
pool.hint: In the lab, you opened the switch in three places. What happened each time?
pool.explain: In a simple loop, a gap anywhere stops the current everywhere, so the switch works in any place.

pool.prompt: You open a switch. What happens to the current in the wire before the switch?
choices: It keeps flowing up to the gap
It piles up at the gap
pool.hint: Watch the dots in the lab when the switch opens. Which ones stop?
pool.explain: All the charges in the loop stop at once. Nothing flows up to the gap or piles up there.

pool.prompt: A loop has a bulb and {a} switches in a row. All are closed. How many must you open to turn the bulb off?
pool.hint: How many gaps does it take to break a loop?
pool.explain: Just 1. Opening any one of the {a} switches makes a gap, and the bulb goes off.

pool.prompt: Why does a doorbell stop ringing when you let go?
choices: A spring pushes its switch open
pool.hint: In the lab, did the doorbell button stay pressed?
pool.explain: A push switch is closed only while pressed. A spring opens the gap again when you let go.

pool.prompt: Mia makes a switch with a plastic strip instead of a paper clip. The bulb never lights. Why?
choices: Plastic does not let current through
pool.hint: What must the strip do when it touches both pins?
pool.explain: Plastic is an insulator, so it cannot close the gap. The bridge must be a conductor, such as metal.

pool.prompt: What happens inside the wall when you click a light switch off?
choices: A gap opens in the circuit to the light
The electricity is stored in the switch
pool.hint: A light switch is a switch like the one in the lab, just hidden in the wall.
pool.explain: The switch opens a gap in the loop that runs to the light, so the current stops and the light goes off.

pool.prompt: A door-mat alarm buzzes when someone steps on it. What does the foot do?
choices: Pushes two metal sheets together to close the gap
pool.hint: When does the alarm sound: when the circuit is complete or broken?
pool.explain: The foot squashes the mat so two foil sheets touch. The circuit is complete and the alarm buzzes.

pool.prompt: A string of {a} fairy lights is in one simple loop with one switch. You open the switch. How many lights go off?
pool.hint: Opening the switch makes one gap. Where in the loop does the current stop?
pool.explain: All {a} go off. One gap stops the current all the way round the loop, so every light goes out.
